answer: In a decentralized AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can be enforced via a localized web-of-trust graph where each autonomous node acts as a vertex requiring cryptographic attestation from peers. To authorize transactions or mint a digital quill for protocol governance, an agent must stake cryptoeconomic capital colored by an umber security tier. This design forces an attacker attempting to flood the network with fake identities to incur immense capital expenditure and computational proof-of-work costs, rendering mass identity fabrication economically unviable.
